narrative.course_description: Software Development using AI examines modern AI-native software development workflows where developers collaborate with coding agents. The course covers configuring developer environments, Model Context Protocol specifications, agent orchestration frameworks, context engineering, and spec-driven development. For advanced undergraduate computer science students, mastering the design, coordination, and evaluation of human-AI collaborative workflows is essential for modern software engineering practice. Students will learn to implement AI-assisted coding workflows, assess executable specifications from natural language requirements, analyze execution traces of iterative agentic loops to diagnose failures, and evaluate the reliability of AI-generated applications using deployment metrics. The course is delivered through lectures, tutorials, practical laboratory sessions, and a comprehensive development project. It is structured specifically as a workflow-oriented engineering course rather than a general introduction to machine learning or a traditional programming course.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The module sequence logically progresses from foundational setup to advanced evaluation. It begins with environment configuration and agent skills (M1–M3), moves to specification and context engineering (M4–M6), advances to iterative development and trace diagnostics (M7–M9), and concludes with automated testing and deployment metrics (M10–M12). This flow ensures students master tool integration before designing complex specifications and debugging agentic loops, building directly upon the software development and unit testing fundamentals acquired in CSE201.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment scheme balances practical application and theoretical understanding. Labs (15%) and assignments (15%) evaluate hands-on tool integration and specification analysis (CO1, CO2). The course project (25%) requires students to collaboratively build, debug, and evaluate a complete AI-assisted application, directly addressing high-level analysis and evaluation outcomes (CO3, CO4). Midsem (20%) and endsem (25%) exams ensure individual accountability and conceptual mastery of loop engineering, context design, and reliability metrics.
narrative.positioning_rationale: This course fills a distinct niche at IIIT-D. Unlike CSE701, which focuses on mining software repositories and machine learning research, or CSE582 and CSE581, which cover traditional software product lines and requirements engineering, this course is AI-native. It also differs from the 2-credit CSE594A by focusing comprehensively on software engineering workflows rather than general scientific agent reasoning, and builds upon the programming foundations of CSE201 without duplicating basic ML concepts from AI501.
